subject: Mathematics
summary: Pair 4 (Dice Predictions) clears the bar with all six categories at 4. The expanded_walkthrough names the gambler's-fallacy / representativeness misconception with three named research citations (Kahneman & Tversky 1972; Fischbein 1975; Konold 1989) and provides three diagnostic-branched recovery_moves (A: 'won't roll 6 again' demo; B: cup-cover for favourite-number bias; C: uniform-distribution-but-can't-predict-mode). Mae's quotable refrain 'Each roll is FRESH — the die FORGETS!' threads through the hook and the consolidation exit_routine as a 3x choral chant with an open-palm wipe gesture. Puppets are explicitly OPTIONAL with substitutes, and a NO-PAPER finger-dice version (child holds 1-6 fingers behind back, partner says STOP) makes the lesson runnable on prep-less days. Action step 6 STRATEGY COMPARE has three pairs share prediction strategies ('guess my favourite' vs. 'roll-and-record-then-predict' vs. 'each face has 1/6 chance'), with Konold (1989) cited for the outcome-orientation → long-run frequency shift. Consolidation prompt 5 is an explicit Day-5 forward-bridge to mode prediction across populations (D2.2 capstone). Worksheet's three parts (12 rolls + mode; second 12 rolls + compare; predict third 12-roll mode + test) faithfully mirror the lesson's station structure, and the early_finisher 100-roll prediction adds a transfer extension. Ship it.
